segments.text: Lesson 32
segments.translation: 第32课

segments.text: A lost ship
segments.translation: 一艘沉没的轮船

segments.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question.
segments.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。

segments.text: Did the crew of the Elkor find what they were looking for? Why?
segments.translation: “埃尔科”号的船员们找到他们要找的东西了吗？为什么？

segments.text: The salvage operation had been a complete failure.
segments.translation: 打捞工作彻底失败了。

segments.text: The small ship, Elkor, which had been searching the Barents Sea for weeks, was on its way home.
segments.translation: 那艘小船“埃尔科”号已经在巴伦支海搜索了几个星期，现在正处于返航途中。

segments.text: A radio message from the mainland had been received by the ship's captain instructing him to give up the search.
segments.translation: 船长接到了来自大陆的电报，指示他放弃搜索。

segments.text: The captain knew that another attempt would be made later, for the sunken ship he was trying to find had been carrying a precious cargo of gold bullion.
segments.translation: 船长深知下次还会再尝试，因为他正试图寻找的那艘沉船上载有一批极其值钱的黄金金锭。

segments.text: Despite the message, the captain of the Elkor decided to try once more.
segments.translation: 尽管接到了电报，但“埃尔科”号的船长还是决定再试一次。

segments.text: The sea bed was scoured with powerful nets and there was tremendous excitement on board when a chest was raised from the bottom.
segments.translation: 他们用强有力的网在海底仔细搜查。当一个大箱子从海底打捞上来时，船上的人变得兴奋异常。

segments.text: Though the crew were at first under the impression that the lost ship had been found, the contents of the chest proved them wrong.
segments.translation: 虽然船员们起初以为那艘失踪的船已经被找到了，但箱子里的东西证明他们弄错了。

segments.text: What they had in fact found was a ship which had been sunk many years before.
segments.translation: 事实上他们找到的是一艘多年前沉没的船。

segments.text: The chest contained the personal belongings of a seaman, Alan Fielding.
segments.translation: 箱子里装的是一个名叫 Alan Fielding 的水手的私人物品。

segments.text: There were books, clothing and photographs, together with letters which the seaman had once received from his wife.
segments.translation: 里面有书、衣服和照片，还有那个水手以前收到的他妻子的来信。

segments.text: The captain of the Elkor ordered his men to salvage as much as possible from the wreck.
segments.translation: “埃尔科”号的船长命令手下人从那艘沉船中尽可能多地打捞东西。

segments.text: Nothing of value was found, but the numerous items which were brought to the surface proved to be of great interest.
segments.translation: 虽然没有找到任何值钱的东西，但打捞上来的众多物品却引起了极大的兴趣。

segments.text: From a heavy gun that was raised, the captain realized that the ship must have been a cruiser.
segments.translation: 船长根据打捞上来的一门沉重的炮意识到，这艘船一定是一艘巡洋舰。

segments.text: In another chest which contained the belongings of a ship's officer, there was an unfinished letter which had been written on March 14th, 1943.
segments.translation: 在另一个装有一名船上军官物品的箱子里，有一封写于1943年3月14日的未写完的信。

segments.text: The captain learnt from the letter that the name of the lost ship was the Karen.
segments.translation: 船长从信中得知，这艘沉船的名字叫“卡伦”号。

segments.text: The most valuable find of all was the ship's log book, parts of which it was still possible to read.
segments.translation: 在所有的发现中，最值钱的东西就是那本航海日志，日志中有些部分仍然可以辨认。

segments.text: From this the captain was able to piece together all the information that had come to light.
segments.translation: 船长根据这些日志拼凑出了所有已曝光的信息。

segments.text: The Karen had been sailing in a convoy to Russia when she was torpedoed by an enemy submarine.
segments.translation: “卡伦”号在随船队开往俄罗斯的途中被敌方的潜艇击沉了。

segments.text: This was later confirmed by a naval official at the Ministry of Defence after the Elkor had returned home.
segments.translation: 在“埃尔科”号回到家乡后，国防部的一位海军官员证实了这一点。

segments.text: All the items that were found were sent to the War Museum.
segments.translation: 所有发现的物品都被送到了战争博物馆。
